item.title: How Tanganyika Won Independence on 9 December 1961
item.dc:creator: Mclean Mbaga
item.description: A clear timeline from German rule and the British mandate to TANU in 1954, the elections, and independence on 9 December 1961, won by talks and votes.
item.content:encoded:
Every 9 December, Tanzanians remember the day their country became free of colonial rule. The date is simple to remember. The road to it was longer, and it is worth knowing step by step. This post gives you a timeline you can trust, with the sources at the end.

The short answer

Tanganyika became independent from Britain on 9 December 1961. It got there through a political party, TANU, led by Julius Nyerere. TANU argued for independence, spoke to the United Nations, and won elections. The sources we opened describe a party, talks and elections, and none describes an armed struggle.

  • 1954: TANU is formed on 7 July.
  • 1955 and 1956: Nyerere speaks to the UN Trusteeship Council in New York.
  • 1958 and 1960: TANU wins elections.
  • 9 December 1961: independence.
  • 1962: Tanganyika becomes a republic.

What was Tanganyika before independence?

For about three decades, the land was part of German East Africa. World History Encyclopedia says Germany ruled the colony from 1885 to 1918 and lost it by defeat in the First World War. EBSCO says that after the war the territory went to the League of Nations, which gave Britain the mandate to rule it. A mandate is a duty to govern a territory on behalf of an international body.

After the Second World War, the arrangement changed. The United Nations research guide says Tanganyika became a Trust Territory under United Kingdom administration, with the trusteeship agreement approved on 13 December 1946.

So by the 1950s, Britain was administering Tanganyika under a UN trusteeship agreement.

7 July 1954: TANU is formed

EBSCO says the Tanganyika African National Union was formed on 7 July 1954, with Julius Nyerere as its president.

TANU's goal was independence. Its route, as the sources describe it, was political: appeals to the UN and elections.

Speaking to the United Nations

EBSCO says Nyerere travelled to New York to address the UN Trusteeship Council twice, in March 1955 and in December 1956.

Think about what that means. The leader of a political party in a trust territory went to New York to make the case for self-rule in front of an international body.

We did not find, in the sources we opened, the exact wording of what he said, so we do not quote it.

1958 to 1960: elections and self-government

EBSCO says TANU won the Legislative Council elections of September 1958 "overwhelmingly". In August 1960 came a general election, after which Nyerere was elected as prime minister of the new government. Wikipedia's article on the territory says TANU won both the 1958 and 1960 elections.

Titles in these years differ between sources. Some call the leader "chief minister" before "prime minister". We have not confirmed the exact dates of each title, so we use the safer wording: by independence, Nyerere was leading the government as prime minister.

We also left out seat counts, because we could not check them in a source we opened.

9 December 1961: independence day

EBSCO says Tanganyika achieved independence on 9 December 1961. The Wikipedia article on the Union of Tanganyika and Zanzibar gives the same date and says Nyerere was Prime Minister.

Other countries moved quickly. The US Office of the Historian says President John F. Kennedy sent a congratulatory message to Nyerere on 9 December 1961, and that the US recognised Tanganyika and set up diplomatic relations that day. The UN's list of members shows that Tanzania, the state that Tanganyika later became part of, was admitted on 14 December 1961. That is five days after independence.

You may have heard a story about why the date was fixed as 9 December. The accounts we saw were one person's memory and did not agree with a UN record on the original date, so we leave it out.

A quick timeline

DateWhat happenedSource
1885 to 1918German rule in German East AfricaWorld History Encyclopedia
After the First World WarLeague of Nations gives Britain the mandateEBSCO
13 December 1946UN approves the trusteeship agreement, with the UK as administering authorityUN research guide
7 July 1954TANU is formedEBSCO
March 1955, December 1956Nyerere addresses the UN Trusteeship CouncilEBSCO
September 1958Legislative Council elections, won overwhelmingly by TANUEBSCO
August 1960General election, Nyerere elected prime minister of the new governmentEBSCO
9 December 1961IndependenceEBSCO, US Office of the Historian
14 December 1961Tanzania admitted to the UNUN member list
1962Republic, with Nyerere as presidentEBSCO

Three words worth knowing

Mandate. A task given to a country by the League of Nations to govern a territory.

Trust Territory. The name the United Nations used for such a territory after 1946. Tanganyika was one, and the UK was its administering authority.

Legislative Council. The law-making body of the territory before independence. EBSCO says TANU won its 1958 elections overwhelmingly.

After independence: the republic and the Union

EBSCO says that in 1962 the country became a republic and Nyerere became president. Wikipedia gives the date of the republican constitution as 9 December 1962. In 1964, Tanganyika joined with Zanzibar. You can read that story in our post on how Tanganyika and Zanzibar became Tanzania.

Why does the peaceful road matter?

Compare it with the earlier chapter. In 1905 to 1907, many communities rose in arms against German rule in the Maji Maji war, and a very large number of people died, mostly from famine. You can read that in our post on the Maji Maji war.

Independence in 1961 came by a different path: organising, speaking and voting. We do not claim that nobody suffered under colonial rule, or that no one was ever hurt in the years before. We only say that the sources we read describe elections and talks, not a war.

Common questions

When did Tanganyika become independent?

On 9 December 1961, according to EBSCO and the other sources below.

When was TANU formed?

On 7 July 1954, with Julius Nyerere as president.

Who ruled Tanganyika before independence?

Germany until the First World War, then Britain, first under a League of Nations mandate and then as the administering authority of a UN Trust Territory.

Is 9 December the same as Union Day?

No. Union Day is on 26 April and marks the 1964 union with Zanzibar.

What to do next

  1. Write the five key dates on one page: 1954, 1955, 1958, 1960 and 1961.
  2. Read the EBSCO summary on Nyerere to see the same story in more detail.
  3. Ask an older relative where they were on 9 December 1961, and note down their story with their name and the date.

Learning how this was done, step by step, helps us value it.

Sources and further reading

  • Julius Nyerere emerges as leader of Tanganyika, EBSCO Research Starters
  • Trust and Non-Self-Governing Territories, United Nations Dag Hammarskjold Library
  • Member States, United Nations
  • Tanzania country page, US Office of the Historian
  • German East Africa, World History Encyclopedia

item.title: How the United Nations Began: From War to the 1945 Charter
item.dc:creator: Mclean Mbaga
item.description: How the United Nations began, from the Atlantic Charter of 1941 to the San Francisco Charter of 1945, and how Tanganyika was linked to it before 1961.
item.content:encoded:
The United Nations was born out of a war that left families everywhere in grief. Its founders wanted a place where countries could argue with words instead of weapons. This post follows how that idea grew, step by step, and ends with the part of the story that touches Tanzania.

The short answer

The United Nations was planned during World War II. Its Charter was signed in San Francisco on 26 June 1945 and came into force on 24 October 1945, which is why 24 October is United Nations Day.

  • The first ideas came in 1941 and 1942, while the war was still going on.
  • Four powers, the United States, the United Kingdom, the Soviet Union and China, drafted the first proposals in 1944.
  • Fifty nations signed the Charter in 1945, and Poland signed later that year, making 51 original members.
  • Tanganyika was a UN trust territory under British administration before it joined the UN on 14 December 1961.

Why did leaders want a new organisation?

Before the UN there was the League of Nations, created after World War I. It did not stop the next world war. By 1945 many leaders agreed that a stronger body was needed.

The Charter itself shows the mood. Its opening words, in the UN's summary, say the peoples of the United Nations are determined to save future generations from war, which brought great suffering twice in one lifetime. We do not quote any figure for the dead, because estimates differ and we have not confirmed one from a UN page. It is enough to say that the loss was enormous, and the founders knew it.

If you want the background to the earlier war, read our post on what caused World War I.

How did the idea grow, from 1941 to 1943?

The UN's own history pages give this timeline.

  • 12 June 1941. Britain, its Dominions and several governments in exile signed the Declaration of St James's Palace in London. It called for cooperation among free peoples after the war.
  • 14 August 1941. US President Franklin Roosevelt and British Prime Minister Winston Churchill issued the Atlantic Charter. Its eighth paragraph spoke of a future "wider and permanent system of general security".
  • 1 January 1942. Twenty-six states at war with the Axis Powers endorsed the Atlantic Charter's principles in the Declaration by United Nations. This was the first official use of the term "United Nations". The UN says Roosevelt coined it.
  • 18 October to 1 November 1943. At the Moscow Conference, the United States, United Kingdom, Soviet Union and China called for a general international organisation to keep peace and security. The UN calls it the first official document to do so.
  • 28 November to 1 December 1943. Roosevelt, Churchill and Stalin met in Tehran and agreed to keep working together during and after the war.

So the name came first as the name of the wartime alliance. Later it became the name of the organisation.

What happened at Dumbarton Oaks, Yalta and San Francisco?

Dumbarton Oaks, 21 August to 7 October 1944. Representatives of the four powers drafted proposals for the new organisation. The final document was issued on 9 October 1944 and became the working paper for the later conference.

Yalta, 4 to 11 February 1945. The leaders agreed on how voting in the Security Council would work. They also called a conference in San Francisco for 25 April 1945.

San Francisco, 25 April to 26 June 1945. The UN says 50 nations sent delegates. Forty-six were invited at first and four more were invited later: the Byelorussian SSR, the Ukrainian SSR, Denmark and Argentina. There were 850 delegates. With advisers and staff the number was 3,500, and more than 2,500 press, radio, newsreel people and observers also came.

The Charter was adopted unanimously on 25 June at the Opera House. It was signed the next day at the Herbst Theatre.

Why do some sources say 50 and others say 51?

Both numbers are right, and each one counts something different. Fifty nations took part in the conference and signed on 26 June. Poland had no representative there, because its new government was announced too late, and a space was left open for it. A Polish government was announced on 28 June, and Poland signed on 15 October 1945. That made 51 original Members.

What happened on 24 October 1945?

A treaty only starts when enough countries approve it at home. The Charter came into force on 24 October 1945, after the five permanent members of the Security Council and a majority of the other signatories deposited their ratifications. The UN says this date is now observed as United Nations Day.

The purposes in Article 1 include keeping international peace and security, building friendly relations between nations, working together on economic, social, cultural and humanitarian problems, and promoting human rights for everyone without distinction of race, sex, language or religion. The UN today lists 193 member countries.

How is Tanzania linked to the story?

Tanganyika did not sign in 1945, because it was not independent. It was a colony under British rule. After World War I it had been a mandate, and after World War II it became a trust territory. The UN's research guide lists Tanganyika as a Trust Territory administered by the United Kingdom, with the trusteeship agreement approved by the General Assembly on 13 December 1946.

The Charter's chapter on trusteeship set out aims. These include helping the people of a territory make progress towards self-government or independence, as suited to the territory and the wishes of its people. It also called for respect for human rights without distinction of race, sex, language or religion.

Tanganyikans used this system to speak for themselves. According to The Citizen, a Tanzanian newspaper, Julius Nyerere presented Tanganyika's case to the UN Trusteeship Council in New York in March 1955 and again in November 1956. The same article says that visiting Trusteeship Council members suggested in 1954 a path of 20 to 25 years to independence, which the nationalist party TANU thought too slow. The article credits Nyerere's arguments with shortening it to about seven years. That is the newspaper's view. We could not confirm from a UN page how much his arguments changed the timetable, so read it as one account.

Tanganyika became independent on 9 December 1961, according to the same article. The UN's list of members gives the admission date of the United Republic of Tanzania as 14 December 1961.

To read more of that story, see how Tanganyika won independence and Julius Nyerere and ujamaa.

Common questions

When was the United Nations founded?

The Charter was signed on 26 June 1945 and came into force on 24 October 1945. The UN says it officially came into existence on that second date.

Who coined the name "United Nations"?

The UN says Roosevelt coined it. It was first used officially in the Declaration by United Nations on 1 January 1942.

What was a trust territory?

It was a territory placed under the UN trusteeship system, run by an administering country and watched by the Trusteeship Council. Tanganyika was one, administered by the United Kingdom.

When did Tanzania join the UN?

The UN member list gives 14 December 1961 as the date of admission.

What to do next

  1. Mark 24 October on your calendar as United Nations Day, and read the Charter's opening words on the UN website.
  2. Compare the dates in this post with your school notes, and check them against the sources below.
  3. Read about Tanganyika's road to independence to see how the trusteeship system fit into it.

History like this reminds us that even after great loss, people sat down and tried to build something better, and you can learn from that.

Sources and further reading

  • San Francisco Conference, United Nations
  • Trust Territories, United Nations Dag Hammarskjöld Library research guide
  • Chapter XII: International Trusteeship System, UN Charter
  • Member States, United Nations
  • How Nyerere's leadership guided Tanganyika to independence in only 7 years, The Citizen

item.title: How to Ask Customers for Reviews Honestly, and Handle Bad Ones
item.dc:creator: Mclean Mbaga
item.description: How to ask customers for reviews with a link or QR code, why you must never pay for them, and how to reply calmly to good and bad reviews.
item.content:encoded:
You work hard to serve people well. Then one day you read a review that says something unkind, and your stomach drops. Or the opposite happens: weeks pass, you serve hundreds of people, and not one of them writes a word.

Both feelings are normal. This post helps with both. It explains how to ask for reviews in a fair way, what you must never do to get them, and how to reply to a bad review without making things worse.

The short answer

Ask every customer, politely, to share their honest experience, and make it easy with a link or a QR code. Never pay, give gifts or trade favours for a review, and never write fake ones. Reply to each review in a calm, short and honest way. Ask permission before you show a customer's words, name or chat to others.

  • Ask in person or by message, right after a good moment of service.
  • Give a simple link or QR code from your profile.
  • Do not offer discounts, free items or any reward for a review.
  • Reply to good and bad reviews politely, and never share private details.
  • Use customer words in your own posts only with their clear permission.

Why do reviews matter so much?

When you buy a phone cover at a stall, you can pick it up and look at it. When you order from a shop you have never visited, you cannot. You have only the pictures, the price and what other people say. A review is a stranger's way of saying "this shop did what it promised" or "it did not".

We cannot say that reviews raise your rank on Google or lift your sales, because we have no firm source for those claims. What we can say is that people often look for them, and that an honest review gives a new customer a reason to trust you. It also gives you something just as useful: a picture of what you do well and where you can improve.

How do I ask: a link, a QR code and a simple message

Google's help pages say you can ask customers to leave a review by sending them to a Google link or having them scan a QR code, and that you can create either one from your Business Profile. If you do not have a profile yet, read our post on how to claim a free Google Business Profile for your shop.

Know this before you ask: customers need to be signed in to a Google Account to post a review. Google says they can create one with an email address that is not Gmail. Some customers will not have an account or will not want to make one. That is fine. Do not push.

Here are some simple ways to ask:

  • At the counter. After a good conversation or a smooth sale, say, "If you were happy with us, would you share a few words online? It helps other people find us. Here is a code you can scan."
  • By message. Send a short, friendly note with the link a day or so after the sale.
  • On a small card or sign. Put a printed QR code near the till or on your receipts.

Here is sample wording you can adapt. It is an example for you to copy, not a real customer comment:

Thank you for buying from us today. If you have a minute, we would be glad to hear how it went, good or not so good. Your honest words help us improve. Here is the link: (your link).

Notice that it asks for honesty, not for five stars. This is our opinion, not a Google rule: the fair habit is to ask everyone, not only the customers who look happy. If you ask only the happy ones, the picture people see becomes less true. Google's pages we read do not name this practice, so check its current rules yourself.

Do not ask a customer who is upset or in a hurry. Fix the problem first. If it is fixed and they want to share what happened, that is their choice.

What must I not do?

This part matters most, because breaking these rules can harm your business.

Do not pay for reviews or reward them. Google's help page is blunt. It says offering free or discounted goods or services in return for reviews is "strictly prohibited". The same applies to offering a reward to change a review, or to get a negative review removed. Google treats that as fake and misleading content. So "Leave us five stars and get 10% off" is not allowed.

Do not write reviews for your own shop, or ask friends to write about visits that never happened. Google says reviews must reflect a genuine experience.

Do not buy reviews, likes or comments from someone else. Other platforms have similar rules. Meta's spam policy, for example, bans trading for engagement and offering anything of value in return for it.

Do not give false information about your goods or services. Tanzania's Fair Competition Act of 2003 has a section against misleading or deceptive conduct in trade (section 15) and a section against false or misleading representations about goods and services (section 16). We read these headings in the copy on the WIPO Lex website. This is not legal advice. If you are unsure whether something you plan to say about your products is allowed, ask a qualified adviser.

Fake praise also hurts you in a quiet way. Once a customer feels a review is fake, they stop trusting every review you have.

How do I reply to a good review and to a bad one?

Replies are public. Anyone who reads reviews can read what you wrote back. Google asks that replies be polite, professional, short and relevant. It also says not to use replies to promote deals.

A good review

A thank-you that says something real is better than a copy-paste line. Google suggests avoiding generic thanks and sharing something useful instead, such as an answer to a question, or an invitation to come back. For example:

Thank you, (name). We are glad the repair was done the same day. Come back any time you need help.

Use your own words each time. If you have no time, a short real reply is better than a long stale one.

A bad review

This is the hard part. Take a breath. Do not answer while you are angry. Leave it for an hour or until the next morning.

Google's advice for negative reviews is practical:

  1. Reply promptly, but calmly. Use the reviewer's name and sign your reply.
  2. Be honest. If you made a mistake, say so. Apologise if an apology is right.
  3. Explain what you can and cannot do. Do not make promises you cannot keep.
  4. Never share private details or attack the person. For a complex problem, invite them to continue by phone or email.
  5. If a review breaks Google's content policies, you can flag it. For example, if it is clearly fake or abusive.

Here is a sample reply. It is only an example of wording, not a real review or answer:

We are sorry the delivery was late, (name). That is not the service we want to give. Please call us on (number) so we can see what went wrong and put it right if we can.

Do not try to hide or delete critical reviews, and do not offer a gift in return for removing one. Google calls that fake and misleading behaviour. A negative review that gets a calm, kind reply can tell other readers more about you than a page of stars. People understand that mistakes happen. They notice how you respond.

Can I share customer words and chat screenshots?

Only with permission. A kind message in your WhatsApp inbox belongs to the person who wrote it. Before you post their words, their photo or a screenshot of the chat:

  • Ask them clearly, and explain where you will show it.
  • Take out names, phone numbers and any details they did not agree to share.
  • Never change what they said.
  • Take it down if they ask you to.

Tanzania has a Personal Data Protection Act. We have not studied it for this post, and this is not legal advice. Asking permission and showing the least personal detail is a respectful habit in any case.

Common questions

How many reviews do I need?

There is no fixed number. Focus on asking every customer fairly and replying to each review. A few honest reviews are better than many bought ones.

What if a customer gives only a low star rating with no words?

You can still reply. Thank them for the feedback, say you would like to learn what went wrong and give a phone number or email. Do not ask them to change the rating.

Can I offer a small gift to thank people for reviewing?

No. Google's help pages say that giving free or discounted goods or services in return for reviews is strictly prohibited. You can thank customers warmly, but do not attach a reward.

Can I remove a review I do not like?

Not just because it is unkind or hurts. If it breaks Google's content policies, for example if it is fake or abusive, you can flag it. Otherwise, reply politely and move on.

What to do next

  1. Create your review link or QR code from your profile, and test it on your own phone.
  2. Write one friendly sentence for asking, and use it with every customer for two weeks.
  3. Write down your rules for replies: stay calm, wait before answering, never share private details.
  4. Read all your reviews once a month and note one thing to improve.

A shop is built from many small acts of trust. One honest review at a time is a good way to earn it.

Sources and further reading

  • Read and reply to reviews, Google Business Profile Help
  • Fake engagement and review policy, Google Business Profile Help
  • Fair Competition Act, 2003 (Tanzania), WIPO Lex
  • Spam, Meta Transparency Centre

Google's rules were checked in November 2026 and can change, so open the pages above for the current wording.
